Nepal doubled its wild tigers — 121 in 2009, 355 in 2022. The National Trust for Nature Conservation says Nepal is the first country to meet that pledge. Rangers, restored corridors and more than 450 community anti-poaching units made it possible. Wild tigers had fallen by 97% in a century, to about 3,200 worldwide by 2010. What would you ask a ranger who helped turn that around? Sources, named on screen: NTNC, 29 July 2022. Story: link in bio (savingplanets.com/Nepal_Tigers.html). Narrated by Archer.
